messages:
alex: hey support, we've got a customer hitting repeated SSE disconnects after upgrading to python-sdk 0.12.3. they see truncated partial outputs and then duplicated tokens when the client reconnects. billing spikes reported for the same request id.

jenn (Support): sorry to hear that — can you paste a minimal repro and the request_id? is this reproducible for the same prompt or intermittent?

alex: happens reliably for this long streaming generation (>512 tokens). small sample prompt attached. request_id: r-8a3f2d. we repro locally with our app and also observed on their prod.

alex: repro steps:
1) pip install redwood-sdk==0.12.3
2) run this script:
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=\"REDACTED\")
resp = client.stream.generate(prompt=\"<long prompt>\")
for chunk in resp:
    print(chunk.text, end=\")
```
3) after ~3-5s connection drops with HTTP/1.1 200 then client reconnect; output resumes but the last ~8 tokens are repeated.

alex: logs (client-side):
```
[sse] connection closed: errno=104 (Connection reset by peer)
[sdk] reconnecting using Last-Event-ID: 00000000000000003
[stream] resumed, received 8 duplicate tokens
```

alex: curl to server record shows the upstream returned 200 and then closed:
```bash
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer KEY\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-redwood-1\"
```

jenn (Support): thanks. two concern buckets: a) client iterator handling in python-sdk when underlying connection resets, b) server-side resume semantics. billing spike could be because resume results in server re-sending tokens that are counted as new. forwarding to eng-runtime + SRE. @sam @maria fyi. :eyes:

sam (Eng Runtime): looking. can you attach the full raw SSE payload and the value of Last-Event-ID? also include X-Request-ID and X-Region headers. sometimes proxies close idle connections and the resume path currently replays from last flush, not last acked token.

maria (SRE): we saw a small jump in token counts for that request_id r-8a3f2d around 2026-03-11T16:12:02Z. capturing backend logs now. what's the customer’s region?

alex: region eu-west-1. attached a pcap and the raw stream. customer also reported higher latency (p99 from 300ms->1.2s) immediately before the drop.

jenn (Support): repro on our side too. quick workaround: set client.stream.buffering=False and client.stream.resume_policy=\"no-replay\" (not ideal but stops duplicates). can you confirm?

sam (Eng Runtime): confirmed workaround stops the duplicate emissions because the client will not attempt a resume — it will start a fresh request. downside is lost continuity and more tokens billed if the app retries full generation. root cause hypothesis: python-sdk's async iterator yields buffered chunks after reconnect while also replayed chunks are streamed from server, so consumer sees duplicates. the iterator GC path can also fire a cancel which triggers a partial flush.

sam (Eng Runtime): quick patch idea: mark last_emitted_offset on the iterator and ignore any resumed tokens with offset <= last_emitted_offset. also change reconnect logic to send Last-Event-ID set to the last acked event id, not last received.

jenn (Support): can you produce a minimal failing unit test and a short mitigation we can give the customer? they asked for a timeline and whether this is a billing exposure.

sam (Eng Runtime): on it. rough mitigation for support to provide: 1) ask customer to set client.stream.resume_policy=no-replay or set client.stream.buffering=False; 2) collect X-Request-ID, Last-Event-ID, and raw SSE file; 3) if billing spike observed, escalate billing team with the request id and timestamps — we will backfill if server-side double-count is confirmed.

maria (SRE): backend note: proxy timeouts at edge were recently lowered to 45s for one tenant — could explain disconnect before client ACK. will revert for that tenant and monitor.

alex: customer wants a patch asap. any ETA on the iterator fix?

sam (Eng Runtime): I can open a PR with tests today (will target 0.12.4) to add last_emitted_offset guard and ensure Last-Event-ID behavior. ETA 48 hours for PR + CP. will link PR here.

jenn (Support): great. I'll pass workaround and ask them to hold billing disputes pending our investigation. adding billing@redwood and eng-runtime to the thread. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: @maria is on call for eng-runtime (rotation).

sam (Eng Runtime): PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/redwood-sdk/pull/421 — includes test case for duplicated tokens on reconnect and manual flag to disable resume.

maria (SRE): rolled backed edge timeout for that tenant and started a short trace session for r-8a3f2d window. initial signs show the client retried within 200ms of the disconnect, which allowed replay to overlap.

jenn (Support): next actions: 1) support to share workaround + ask raw traces; 2) eng-runtime to land patch + ship 0.12.4; 3) billing to hold dispute until we confirm root cause.

alex: thanks all. I'll notify the customer and attach the workaround. will upload full traces to the ticket.

sam (Eng Runtime): will follow up in PR and post-release changelog.

jenn (Support): keeping this thread open until patched.
